dedupe_keys.name: japan hourly expected onshore wind generation reconstruction

description: Waseda University and the Central Research Institute of Electric Power Industry publish a reconstruction of expected onshore wind generation in Japan. It contains hourly per-unit output estimates from 1958 to 2012 on an approximately 5 km grid. Dynamically downscaled atmospheric reanalysis supplies the weather conditions; a nonparametric machine-learning model calibrates spatial and meteorological predictors against observed wind-farm outputs. Zenodo lists annual TAR.GZ archives containing NetCDF files and accompanying documentation. Version 1.2 changes the post-processing model’s hyperparameter tuning. Access is open and free under CC-BY-4.0, and the provider suggests Climate Data Operators for working with the files. The principal limitation is that these are reconstructed expected generation profiles, not measurements of the historical Japanese fleet. Modellers could use the time series to explore spatial diversification, low-wind episodes or capacity choices in electricity simulations, after checking per-unit conventions and grid alignment. The resource complements turbine-location inventories by supplying weather-dependent generation behaviour. No files were downloaded or numerical performance reproduced.
